newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn cabinet backs new German troops for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Bonn cabinet backs new German troops for Bosnia.

text.p: The German cabinet on Wednesday approved the assignment of up to 3,300 soldiers to NATO's follow-up force to the IFOR peacekeepers in Bosnia, government spokesman Peter Hausmann said.

Acccepting a joint proposal by Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, the cabinet agreed Germany could pledge ground, air and naval units for the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) due to replace the Implementation Force (IFOR) on December 20.

It emphasised that parliament must first approve the mission, for which the cabinet set no time limit. The Bonn legislature looks likely to approve the renewed Bosnian mission in a session scheduled for December 13.
The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) have spoken out in favour of a further German role in the peace-keeping force and many of the pacifist Greens also seem ready to back it.
Bonn had about 4,000 troops in the IFOR mission but kept them in Croatia because of concerns they could antagonise Bosnian Serbs if they were stationed in Bosnia proper.
Deployment of German troops to the Balkans is sensitive because of their World War Two occupation of Yugoslavia.

But Bonn changed its mind and decided to deploy its SFOR troops on the ground in Bosnia after the IFOR mission went smoothly and local leaders urged Germany to take a full part in the peace-keeping effort.
Hausmann said the German army contingent would include reconnaissance units, engineers, electronic surveillance specialists, medics and logistics units.
German pilots would continue to fly transport planes and Tornado reconnaissance jets while its sailors would continue to man NATO ships in the region, Hausmann said.
Only professional soldiers and conscripts who volunteer for the mission would be sent to Bosnia, he added.
